key_insight: Menopausal timing showed a nonlinear association with blood NfL and a linear association with GDF-15 in older women, suggesting links to neuroaxonal injury and systemic stress rather than cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: These observational biomarker associations may inform research into menopause and dementia biology but do not establish dementia risk or guide treatment.
method: Analyzed U.S. Health and Retirement Study participants aged 65 or older using blood collected in 2016.
Modeled self-reported spontaneous menopause timing against NfL, GFAP, p-tau181 and GDF-15, adjusting for sociodemographic and health factors.
Evaluated APOE ε4 effect modification and separately examined hysterectomy history.
evidence_signal: Among 893 women without hysterectomy, later menopause between ages 50–55 was associated with lower NfL (−0.031 SD/year; 95% CI −0.051 to −0.011); GFAP and p-tau181 associations were not statistically significant.
watch_item: Self-reported reproductive history, unmeasured oophorectomy status and observational biomarker data limit causal interpretation and inference about clinical dementia.
paper_title: Age at Menopause and Dementia Risk: Blood-Based Biomarker Evidence from a US National Study
